text.p: Britain's Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc on Monday announced they would merge to form a new company called GMG Brands.

The companies said the merger would create a major new force in international food and drinks and deliver significant cost savings. Shareholders in GrandMet, which owns Burger King and food group Pillsbury, along with drinks interests, will own 52.7 percent of the new company.
The deal includes a capital repayment to shareholders of not less than 60 pence per share, worth some 2.4 billion pounds.

On Friday's share price, the combined value of the group was 20.61 billion pounds ($33.5 billion), making it the seventh largest food and drinks company worldwide and Britain's eighth largest quoted company.

The merger will also create the world's leading branded spirits and wine company with combined spirits sales of over 100 million cases, bringing together brands like GrandMet-owned Smirnoff vodka and Cinzano with Guinness owned Johnnie Walker whisky and Gordon's gin.
